text:
maya: quick heads-up — I ran a small bring-up sweep for Llama-2-13B (v2.0 weights) quantized q8x4 and int8x4 across A100 / H100 in us-west, eu-west, and ap-southeast. posting raw notes + a tiny command so folks can reproduce. :mag:
simon: awesome, curious about prefill vs decode split and tokens/sec. did you test kernel fallbacks? :eyes:
maya: yes. baseline config: batch=1, seq_in=512, gen=256, beam=1, kv-cache on. used our runtime with kernel selection enabled (cutlass -> triton -> aten fallback order). command I ran:

```bash
./bench_infer --model llama2-13b --quant q8x4 --gpu ${GPU} --batch 1 --seq 512 --gen 256 --kernels auto --runs 200
```

bench-bot: summary (per-run median, prefilling accounted):

- H100 (p4d-like driver) q8x4 us-west: prefill latency 180ms, decode step 9.2ms, tokens/sec ~ 1.8k, $/1M tokens = $18.2
- A100 (a100-80GB) q8x4 us-west: prefill latency 240ms, decode step 12.6ms, tokens/sec ~ 1.3k, $/1M tokens = $25.6

ryan: whoa H100 is ~40% faster on tokens/sec here. are those steady-state numbers or include cold KV misses?

maya: numbers are steady-state after initial warmup for these settings. KV warmup measured separately — hitrate was ~99.2% in this synthetic run. prefill dominated on A100 (more kernel swaps, larger prefill > decode ratio). H100 used cutlass kernels for both prefill/decode mostly; A100 fell back to triton for some attention sizes which cost ~+15–20% on decode.

devon: did you try int8x4? sometimes int8 gives better dollars but regresses quality.

maya: ran int8x4 too — throughput +22% on H100, +18% on A100 vs q8x4. however, LM perplexity delta shows small regression (~0.6 ppl) on an eval prompt set. quality vs cost tradeoff flag. int8 run example snippet:

```csv
gpu,gtype,quant,prefill_ms,decode_ms,tokens_per_sec,dollars_per_1M
H100,int8x4,13b,150,7.5,2200,14.8
A100,int8x4,13b,200,9.8,1600,20.6
```

olivia: regional deltas? any network/placement weirdness in ap-southeast?

maya: ap-southeast H100 numbers drop ~8% tokens/sec vs us-west — likely GPU queueing (we're on a smaller slab there) and slightly older driver/kernel set. eu-west sits between the two. P99 latency: us-west H100 p99 decode ~18ms, ap-south p99 ~24ms. suggestions: pin traffic to larger H100 slab for latency-sensitive workloads.

simon: kernel choice notes important. did you capture which layers used aten fallback on A100? could matter for 13B layer widths.

maya: yes — layer groups 9, 18, 27 hit aten fallback on A100 with q8x4 (attention size 256 windows). H100 handled those with cutlass fast-path. We should add a runtime heuristic: if fallback count > X then prefer H100 or change kernel ordering to prefer triton for those layer sizes.

ryan: can you push the CSVs + the small script to reproduce to the shared bucket? I want to run same config against the dedicated pool.

maya: uploading now to s3://redwood-bench/2712345678/ — files: run_meta.csv, kernel_hits.log, env.txt. Note: env.txt contains driver versions (H100: 22.12, A100: 22.7) — that may explain part of the perf gap.

devon: TL;DR for product — H100 gives ~30–40% tokens/sec uplift and ~25–30% lower $/1M tokens on q8x4 for Llama-2-13B for our configs; int8 improves cost further but watch small quality regressions. regional and driver differences can swing p99. Recommendation: default new L2-13B traffic to H100 for low-latency tiers, add an autoscale policy to route to A100 for lower-cost tiers with cached-prefill important to hit econ targets. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

olivia: perfect. will add short note to the onboarding doc and flag the kernel-fallback heuristic in the runtime backlog. thanks maya + bench-bot! :clap:
